title: Pathfinder: High-Resolution Control-Flow Attacks Exploiting the Conditional Branch Predictor
problem: High-performance CPUs expose conditional branch predictor state (path history register and prediction history tables) to exploitation through microarchitectural side-channel attacks. Attackers can leak entire control flow histories of victim programs and launch high-resolution transient execution attacks by reading and writing to branch predictor state.
motivation: Branch predictor exploitation enables recovery of sensitive information including cryptographic keys and program control flow patterns, compromising CPU security guarantees.
method: The attack exploits the conditional branch predictor—the CPU component that predicts which direction conditional branches in code will go. Read operations extract the path history register (recording which branches were taken) and prediction history tables (storing predictions for each branch), revealing the exact sequence of branches the victim program executed. Write operations modify the predictor state to force speculative execution (running code speculatively to save time) of unintended code, allowing attackers to leak secrets. Practical attacks recover control flow from libjpeg image processing routines and extract cryptographic keys from AES implementations.
key_novelty: First exploitation of branch predictor read and write operations to leak control flow history and enable high-resolution transient execution attacks.
contributions: Attack primitives for reading and writing conditional branch predictor state (PHR and PHTs)
Control flow history recovery attack with practical secret image extraction from libjpeg
High-resolution transient execution attack framework enabling AES cryptographic key recovery
Demonstration of branch predictor state as an exploitable microarchitectural side channel

metrics.accuracy: successful cryptographic key recovery from AES
metrics.other: control flow history recovery and secret image extraction
